prompt: main takes two i32 arguments and returns their sum (wrapping mod 2^32).
main takes one i32 argument and returns its absolute value.
main takes x, lo, hi and returns x clamped to [lo, hi].
main takes n >= 0 and returns 1+2+...+n using a loop.
main takes n >= 0 and returns n! computed by a recursive helper gene.
main takes n >= 0 and returns the n-th Fibonacci number (fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1), computed iteratively.
main takes three i32 arguments and returns the smallest.
main takes n and returns 1 if n is prime, else 0 (n < 2 is not prime).
main reads the input list with READ and returns its maximum (the list has 1..100 elements).
main reads the input list, writes it reversed with WRITE, and returns the element count.
main reads the input list and returns how many elements are even.
main takes no arguments, loads the string "hello world" with SLOAD and returns its byte length via SLEN.
main takes no arguments, prints exactly "hi\n" using SLOAD+PRINT, and returns 0.
main takes two arguments, stores them in STRUCT point fields x and y, and returns 2*x + y.
main takes n (1..90), computes fib(n) using wide i64 registers (fib(1)=1, fib(2)=1), and returns 1 if fib(n) equals fib(90), else 0. Compare with WEQ against WLOAD w3 2880067194370816120.
main takes one argument n, fills a local ARRAY of 8 with a[i] = i+1 for i in 0..7 (ignore n), then returns the sum of all 8 elements (36).

main takes a and b (b != 0). Compute q = a/b truncated toward zero and r = a - q*b (so r has the sign of a; C semantics, NOT floor division). Write q and r as a 2-element output list with WRITE and return q + r.
main takes n >= 0. Start h = 5381 and repeat n times: h = h*33 + 7, keeping h a signed i32 (wrap mod 2^32 EVERY iteration, printed signed at the end). Return h.
main takes a and b and returns gcd(|a|, |b|) by Euclid's algorithm. gcd(0, 0) = 0.

main reads the input list and returns the number of sign changes between consecutive NONZERO elements: compare each nonzero element's sign with the sign of the most recent nonzero element before it; zero elements are skipped entirely (they break nothing and count nothing).

main reads the input list of n elements. Split it into a first half of floor(n/2) elements and a second half of the rest. Write with WRITE: the two halves interleaved, alternating and starting with the first half; when the first half runs out, append the remaining second-half elements. Return n.
main takes a, b, c (i32, |a|,|b| <= 2000000000). Compute a*b - c in 64-bit (the product can overflow i32) and return 1 if the exact 64-bit result fits in a signed i32, else 0.
main takes no arguments. Load the string "hello codons" with SLOAD and return the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in it.

main reads the input list (non-empty) and run-length encodes it: maximal runs of equal values become pairs value,count. Write the flattened pairs with WRITE (e.g. 1,1,2,2,2,3 -> 1,2,2,3,3,1) and return the number of pairs.
main takes n >= 0 and returns its binary-reflected Gray code: n XOR (n shifted right by 1).
